name: Hypersonic Titanium Grid Fins
summary: Four lattice aerodynamic control surfaces mounted around the upper Stage 1 interstage.
function: Steer the descending first-stage booster across supersonic, transonic, and subsonic regimes by generating lateral lift and aerodynamic roll/pitch/yaw authority toward the landing pad.
materials: Single-piece forged and machined titanium alloy (uncoated), able to survive hypersonic reentry heating without ablative thermal paint.

specs.label: Fin Span (each)
specs.source: Public Block 5 titanium grid fin geometry

specs.label: Max Commanded Deflection
specs.source: Public Falcon 9 grid fin deflection estimate

history: Early reusable Falcon 9 boosters used coated aluminum grid fins that melted or charred on high-energy GTO entries. SpaceX introduced single-piece cast/forged titanium grid fins in 2017 (Iridium-2) and standardized them on Block 5.
sources: NASA / Public Aerospace Grid Fin Aerodynamics Literature
